question: If \(F(n+1)=\dfrac{2F(n)+1}{2}\) for \(n=1,\) \(2,\) \(\ldots,\) and \(F(1)=2,\) then \(F(101)\) equals:
solution:
First simplify the recurrence:
\[
F(n+1)=\frac{2F(n)+1}{2}=F(n)+\frac12.
\]
Thus every increase of 1 in the index adds \(\frac12\) to the value. Going from \(F(1)\) to \(F(101)\) takes \(101-1=100\) such increases, so
\[
F(101)=2+100\left(\frac12\right)=\boxed{52}.
\]
The answer is choice D.
